- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off sentiment not fully priced.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in history + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a slight upward bias to counteract pessimism.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; increase initial forecast slightly to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 50% recent sentiment, 50% historical) for correction.
